The dried inflorescence of the breadfruit tree is burned in some
parts of the world to repel biting insects. ARS scientists are
studying the compounds inside this interesting flower to find out
what it contains and whether it might lead them to new repellents.

The masthead staff are the ARS Information Staff, every article byline is ARS (Ann Perry, Dennis O'Brien, Marcia Wood, Sandra Avant), and the page-2 Forum is by Daniel Strickman, ARS National Program Leader. All 24 printed photo numbers (D2619-4 through D2700-2 and K5657-3; photographers Peggy Greb, Stephen Ausmus, Seth Britch, Brad Fritz, Regis Lefebure, Neil Sanscrainte and Dong Wang) were resolved on 2026-09-17 in the ARS Image Gallery (https://www.ars.usda.gov/oc/images/photos/nov12/<id>/), with photographers matching the printed credits. The gallery rights page (https://www.ars.usda.gov/oc/images/copyright/, checked 2026-09-17) says its photos are copyright-free, public domain unless otherwise indicated, may not be used to infer or imply ARS endorsement of any product, company, or position, and asks for credit to the Agricultural Research Service. The masthead also states no endorsement by USDA is implied. Uncredited elements are the flag treatments on pages 1, 2 and 14 (the cover photo is D2700-2), small holly ornaments on the index pages 22-23, and the USDA, ARS and 150 Years marks and mailing panel on page 24.
